title: New AI modeling approach predicts atom movement in solid-state reactions
excerpt: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory researchers built an AI model that couples thermodynamics with atom-transport kinetics to simulate solid-state reaction pathways in minutes, predicting intermediates, final products and impurities. It reproduced decades of barium-titanium oxide experiments, pointing to faster, higher-purity materials synthesis.
rationale: Materials synthesis planning drops from trial-and-error months to minutes, and the model names the impurities you will actually get - directly usable by any lab making new compounds.

title: AI-designed SARS-CoV-2 variants escape prevalent antibodies
excerpt: École Normale Supérieure and Institut Pasteur researchers built EscapeMap, a generative AI framework that designs heavily mutated but still functional SARS-CoV-2 spike variants by balancing sequence viability, ACE2 affinity and immune selection. Most AI-generated variants escaped prevalent antibodies, giving a way to stress-test therapeutics against future strains.
rationale: Generative models now design plausible future viral strains, turning antibody and vaccine design into something you can pressure-test before the variant exists.

title: Why the legendary Erdős problems are falling to AI
excerpt: AI models have begun knocking down long-standing problems posed by Paul Erdős, and mathematicians are trying to work out why this particular corpus is falling first. The piece treats the Erdős problems as a natural test bed for how far machine-generated proof search can go, and what it means for the rest of math.
rationale: The clearest read yet on which kinds of open problems machine proof search actually cracks, and why - useful calibration for anyone judging AI reasoning claims.

title: AI learns to build quantum circuits for drug molecules, cutting design time by orders of magnitude
excerpt: Quantinuum, NVIDIA and Pfizer researchers combined a transformer language model with reinforcement learning to generate molecular ground-state quantum circuits in a single inference step, thousands of times faster than ADAPT-VQE at matching or better accuracy. They demonstrated it on Quantinuum's Helios machine using the drug molecule imipramine.
rationale: A transformer replaces the slowest step of quantum chemistry with one inference pass, demonstrated on real hardware with a real drug molecule rather than a toy system.

title: AI scribes in medical education: learning tool or cognitive crutch?
excerpt: Medical schools are deciding whether students may use AI scribes that auto-generate clinical notes. Hospitals adopted them to cut burnout, but educators warn that offloading the act of writing a differential removes the cognitive struggle that builds diagnostic reasoning.
rationale: The sharpest live case of automation removing the productive struggle that builds expertise - a question every field automating its documentation now faces.
